title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals deployed AI-generated deepfake videos and fake social media profiles to impersonate a real immigration attorney and defraud immigrants. The scam used hundreds of accounts across multiple platforms offering fraudulent legal services, with fabricated testimonials and specific pricing. The system succeeded because victims had no way to verify whether they were communicating with the actual attorney, and the AI-generated content was convincing enough to extract money through digital payment methods.

This is an impersonation attack enabled by generative AI. The failure point was not in the AI system's design for its intended purpose, but in its use to create fraudulent identity. Social media platforms' verification and removal systems caught instances only after the attorney himself noticed the fraud and hired a specialist company to identify fake accounts. What would have prevented damage: either robust identity verification on the platforms before accounts could operate at scale, or the ability to detect and remove deepfake content automatically before victims encountered it.

It is not established whether the criminals who created the scam operated from any particular jurisdiction, what their total proceeds were, or what consequences they faced.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an extensive artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating Leal to defraud immigrants seeking legal assistance. These deepfake videos falsely offer services like US residency assistance for $2,200 and testimonials from supposed clients who obtained legal status through his help. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office about services he never provided.

Since noticing suspicious activity in October, the problem has dramatically escalated over the past three months. Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to WhatsApp where fraudsters send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the source of the fraud. He warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and avoid paying for immigration benefits through digital payment apps.
